Subjective:
- Chief complaint: Left-sided headache that woke patient at approximately 5:30 AM; headache still present at time of consult.
- Headache description: Severe pain on the left side of the head, different from prior headaches which were less severe and typically frontal and bilateral.
- Associated symptoms: Mild sensitivity to bright light causing eye soreness, initial dizziness which has subsided, no nausea, no neck stiffness, no fever.
- Headache onset: This morning; woke patient from sleep.
- Headache modifiers: Slight worsening when lying down initially, then slight improvement when comfortable.
- Treatment attempted: Paracetamol taken this morning without relief.
- Past medical history: Anxiety diagnosed two years ago; no other illnesses reported.
- Medications: Currently taking Sertraline (dose/route/frequency not documented); Paracetamol taken this morning for headache.
- Allergies: None known.
- Family history: No migraines; mother has history of anxiety; no physical illnesses reported.
- Social history: Lives with partner, non-smoker, owns a cat.
- Lifestyle: Exercises by running three times per week; diet described as "OK" but not particularly healthy.
- Psychosocial context: Work-related stress with backlog of work and late nights for about two months; occasional frustration; no current suicidal ideation.

Objective:
- No physical examination findings available due to teleconsultation.
- No vital signs or investigations performed during consult.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Headache, left-sided:
   - Likely diagnosis: Tension-type headache versus migraine.
   - Differential diagnosis: Migraine due to unilateral presentation and photophobia; tension headache related to stress and anxiety.
   - Investigations planned: Consider blood tests and further evaluation if no improvement after initial management.
   - Treatment planned: Initiate Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) as first-line analgesia; continue Paracetamol if desired.
   - Management advice: Emphasize adequate hydration (1.5-2 liters fluids daily, excluding coffee/tea) and ensuring 7-8 hours of sleep nightly.
   - Non-pharmacological: Advise reducing work-related stress; consider taking time off work (self-certified sick leave recommended for about one week).
   - Referral planned: Provide information about local counseling services for stress management and anxiety support.
   - Follow-up: Review in one week to assess response and consider further investigations or management.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements: No documented vital signs; no neurological examination findings; medication dose/frequency for Sertraline and Ibuprofen not specified.
- No internal conflicts noted.
- Transcript quality: Clear and audible, no significant issues affecting information extraction.
